caption:
THAT’S A WRAP: EPISODE 2 🌮 

QUINOA WRAPS made with just quinoa, water and salt 🤌🏼

These are incredibly easy to make and honestly there’s something so satisfying about making your own wraps/tortillas 🥹

They’re perfect to wrap up your favourite fillings, use them for tacos or with some curry or even (my personal favourite) spread some cream cheese in, roll it up and *chef’s kiss* 🤌🏼

Don’t forget to SAVE this recipe for later 😘

(Makes 4-5 medium wraps or 3 large wraps - double quantities for more 👏🏼)

- 100g uncooked quinoa
- 125ml water
- 1/2 tsp salt

1. Rinse quinoa then leave to soak for at least 3 hours (I like to put them in water before bed then make the wraps in the morning).
2. Drain and rinse the soaked quinoa.
3. Add quinoa, 125ml water and salt to a blender and blend until smooth.
4. Scoop 1/4 cup of the mixture into a non-stick pan (spray with cooking spray just in case) and spread to the edges of your pan. Leave for 3-4 minutes or until the bottom is cooked, flip and cook for another minute or so. 
5. Store at room temperature for up to 3 days or in the fridge for up to a week. 

TOP TIP: run some cold water into your pan and rinse to cool down your pan between cooking each wrap. This makes spreading them into a tortilla much easier!

caption:
Who knew makhana could get this chatpata? 

This pani puri-style makhana is my latest snack hack for kids. Makhana is naturally rich in calcium, iron, and antioxidants, making it one of the best snacks to support growing bones and boost immunity 

This one is perfect for tiffins, movie nights, or anytime snack cravings :) 

Recipe: 
- In an air fryer, dry 1 bowl curry leaves, 1 bunch mint leaves & 1 bowl coriander individually at 180*c for 10-15mins
- They should become nice and crisp
- Now grind them all together with black salt, 4-5 peppercorns, chaat Masala, pani puri masala and some mishri (rock sugar) 
- Dry roast 2 bowls of makhana
 Then heat 2 tbsp ghee, add 2 tbsp of the masala and finally the makhana. Mix well till the masala coats the makhana and it’s ready.

caption:
Apple Overnight Oats - Save Recipe Below

Very popular with clients as they can be easily taken to work. Works best if done the night before so the chia and flax can absorb moisture. Great fibre, protein, minerals and fats in particular.

Nutrition - 500 kcal (24P, 67C, 14C) + 14F

100g grated apple (a large one)
40g oats
10g chia seeds
10g flax (ground)
10g honey 
100ml milk (2%)
125g Greek yogurt (5%)
1/2 tsp cinnamon 

Just grate the apple throw it all in and mix it well. If chasing protein use 0% yogurt. I prefer 5%. Adjust the portion as you need. I find glass Tupperware works best (Mason Jars)
